messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] KV_CACHE_PAGING_RATE_HIGH on pool rwd-infer-eu-2. Affected models: gptq-int8 / awq-int8. 95th latency and disk I/O spiking. Pager: alice.

alice: I'm on it — grabbing dashboards/logs.

alice: quick gut check: continuous-batching workers for cg-12 show KV size per-request jumped ~6x around 03:08 UTC. eviction rate skyrocketed.

bob: seeing the same on perf dashboards. @miguel did the kernel-selector change go to cg-12 this morning? (ref commit ab12f3)

miguel: yep, we rolled runtime kernel selector change at ~03:10 UTC that prefers AVX2 int8 kernels. early telemetry indicates that selection path allocates larger KV buffers for gptq/awq profiles. reproducing locally.

tara: also seeing prefix cache churn and higher token costs for some prompt shapes. :grimacing:

sanjay: support already received two P1 tickets from acme-saas and nova-analytics complaining about high latency/timeouts. tagging them.

alice: mitigation plan (short): 1) disable continuous batching on cg-12 2) revert kernel-selector heuristic for that pool 3) apply temporary max_kv_entries cap for int8 models 4) throttle bursts to pool. Doing 1+2 now.

deploy-bot: action: rwdctl pool update cg-12 --continuous-batching=false -> started.

alice: running commands:
```bash
rwdctl pool update cg-12 --continuous-batching=false
rwdctl runtime kernel-select --pool cg-12 --policy revert-2026-03-15
rwdctl pool set-config cg-12 --max-kv-entries=2000000
```

deploy-bot: disable continuous-batching: success (8/8 nodes). kernel-select revert queued to canary.

bob: also setting flow-control to reduce incoming concurrency to 50 for that pool to limit burst amplification.

miguel: kernel revert landed on canary (2/8 nodes). canary logs show KV size drop ~70% for gptq-int8. good signal.

alice: measuring tail latencies on canary traffic — 95p dropped from ~2.1s to ~1.0s. looks promising.

tara: note for follow-up: AWQ quant profiles allocate slightly different KV layout, need separate regression test. adding to eng-ml backlog.

sanjay: drafting CS update now:
- Impact: elevated latency and paging for customers using int8/gptq models. ~3 customers reported.
- Mitigation: reverted kernel selector, disabled continuous batching on cg-12, applied kv cap, throttled pool.
- Next steps: full rollback verification, reproduce locally, postmortem.

helen: joining — will collect artifacts and help with postmortem. please save logs: `/var/log/rwd/pool-cg-12/kernel-select.log`, `s3://rwd-ops/kvcache/spike/1845012345/*`

alice: handing off monitoring to bob at 1845014000. I'm going to step away for 20m but will be reachable.

bob: taking over. watching infra & customer tickets. if 95p > 1.5s we will fallback to smaller int8 quant variants and open a maintenance window.

miguel: created repro ticket for eng-ml w/ steps + artifacts: ENG-ML-1974 (include model, prompt, seq length, kernel trace). will test AWQ/GPTQ differences.

deploy-bot: kernel-select revert: rollout completed (8/8) — success.

alice: confirmed: overall traffic 95p latency back to baseline for most routes. eviction rates decreasing. leaving alert to auto-close in 30m if stable. :thumbsup:

sanjay: sent outbound to affected customers: "We identified and mitigated an operational regression related to int8 kernel selection that caused elevated latency and cache paging. The service is stable; we'll follow up with a detailed incident report."

bob: creating incident tracker INC-2026-048 for root-cause and impact calc.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity=high -> mitigated. linked_incident=INC-2026-048.

alice: good job team. follow-up action items: add unit/regression tests for kernel selector + kv footprint, add metric alert for per-request KV allocation, and add a rollout guard for kernel-selection changes.

helen: noted. scheduling postmortem sync for tomorrow.

bob: closing loop here — will keep monitoring and update ticket. thanks.
